When a visitor follows a public collection, we send an email after new items are added. The email is meant to give followers a useful summary, rather than a separate alert for every item. Additions made within the same hour are grouped into one email. If several people add items during that hour, the follower still receives just the one update for those additions.

Following and email preferences are separate. Someone can continue to follow a collection while turning off collection emails. In that case, new items remain available in the collection, but we do not send that person an email about them. The preference applies even if they followed the collection before switching emails off.

The collection owner does not receive a separate owner copy of these updates. An owner who wants the same email as other followers needs to follow the collection and leave collection emails on. This often comes up when an owner sees that colleagues received an update and assumes theirs went missing.
rows.objective: Rewrite this feature explanation for a help page so readers can see when an email is sent and the two exceptions. Keep the hour-long grouping rule.

When a visitor follows a public collection, we send them an email after new items are added. The email is meant to give followers a useful summary, rather than a separate alert for every item.

**When an email is sent**

Additions made within the same hour are grouped into one email. If several people add items during that hour, the follower still receives just the one update for those additions.

**Two exceptions**

1. **Followers who have turned off collection emails.** Following and email preferences are separate. Someone can continue to follow a collection while turning off collection emails. In that case, new items remain available in the collection, but we do not send that person an email about them. The preference applies even if they followed the collection before switching emails off.

2. **The collection owner.** The owner does not receive a separate owner copy of these updates. An owner who wants the same email as other followers needs to follow the collection and leave collection emails on. This often comes up when an owner sees that colleagues received an update and assumes theirs went missing.

We're preparing a note for teams that borrow the portable display kit. Right now the note tells people to return it to the usual place by the end of the day. That sounds simple until a team uses the kit for an evening event. The storage room may close before the event is over, so a borrower could be following the event plan and still be unable to make that deadline. The note should describe a return window that people can actually use.

The proposed rule is to return the kit by the following business day, when the storage room is open. The exact closing time of the room is not in this brief, and hours may differ by site. Please direct borrowers to check their site's posted storage-room hours instead of supplying a single clock time. The note should also avoid implying that every site opens at the same time. A borrower finishing an evening event needs to know the next step without guessing whether an after-hours return is expected.

Before returning the kit, staff should pack the display, stand, and two cables in its case. Listing the pieces matters because they are used together and can be separated during setup or packing. A quick check while closing the case will make it easier to tell the desk whether a part is missing. The note does not need a lengthy inventory procedure; it just needs a clear reminder of what belongs in the case.

If a cable is missing, staff should still return the kit by the stated window and report the missing part to the desk. They should not hold the rest of the kit while looking for the cable. The desk needs the report so the next borrower can be warned before planning to use it. Keep those two actions together in the note: return what is available, and tell the desk what is absent.
rows.objective: Draft a practical borrower note that resolves the return-time confusion and lists the packing and missing-part steps. The storage-room hours are not supplied, so refer to posted local hours without guessing a closing time.
rows.outputA:
Portable display kit: return and packing note

Please return the kit to the usual place by the following business day, when the storage room is open. Earlier guidance said to return it by the end of the day. That doesn't work for a team using the kit at an evening event, because the storage room may close before the event is over. A borrower could be following the event plan and still be unable to make that deadline.

Storage-room hours may differ by site, so check your site's posted storage-room hours. Don't assume every site opens at the same time. If your event ends in the evening, the next step is to return the kit the following business day. No after-hours return is expected.

Before returning the kit, pack the display, stand, and two cables in its case. These pieces are used together and can get separated during setup or packing, so take a quick look as you close the case. That makes it easier to tell the desk if something is missing. You don't need a full inventory, just a check that those pieces are in the case.

If a cable is missing, still return the kit within the window above, and report the missing part to the desk. Don't hold the rest of the kit while you look for the cable. The desk needs your report so the next borrower can be warned before planning to use it. Return what you have, and tell the desk what is absent.

The new marking process was intended to reduce the time between submission and feedback. Under the previous arrangement, all assignments went through a single coordinator, even where only one tutor was qualified to mark them. The revised process sends assignments directly to the relevant tutor, with the coordinator monitoring progress through a shared register.

During the first term, the median turnaround fell from 18 days to 12 days. However, the number of assignments also fell from 164 to 121, and two tutors had fewer teaching hours than in the previous term. The process change may have contributed to the improvement, but these figures do not establish its individual effect.

Tutors reported that the register was easy to use once they understood when to update it. The first guidance note did not explain whether an assignment should be marked complete when the grade was entered or when feedback was released. That ambiguity caused some records to appear finished too early. A revised note now specifies the release of feedback.

Our recommendation is to retain the process for another term and compare results when the assignment volume is closer to its usual level. We should also check a sample of completed records against actual release dates. A faster-looking register is useful only if it reflects the student's experience.
